title: Per-tenant bundled SLOs with shadow-traffic validation and prioritized degradation policy
creator: Alyssa Chen
description: Goal: Define and operationalize a tenant-scoped SLO bundle (latency + quality + availability) and an experimental validation flow that uses shadow traffic to verify SLO mappings prior to enforcement. Motivation: Some customers have tight latency expectations while others prioritize output quality; we need per-tenant contracts that map to actionable error budgets, and a safe way to validate degradation rules before they affect real traffic. Scope: - Define SLIs and the composition rules for per-tenant bundles. - Specify error-budget math and burn-rate semantics at tenant granularity. - Design shadow-traffic validation and rollout gating. - Define tenant-prioritized degradation and circuit-breaker behavior (regional and global). Non-goals: Full UI in Console (this ticket is policy + infra + metrics + canary automation).
proposal: 1) SLI definitions: - latency_sli: P95 request latency on inference path (end-to-end, client-visible). - quality_sli: per-tenant quality score averaged over a canonical prompt set (e.g., BLEU-like or task-specific eval metric) reported as a 7-day moving average. - availability_sli: success rate (HTTP 200s with model response) over 1h windows. 2) Bundled SLO: weighted composite SLO = 0.5 * latency_target + 0.4 * quality_target + 0.1 * availability_target (weights configurable per tenant). 3) Error budget: compute as (1 - composite_slo) over a rolling 30d window with daily burn-rate. 4) Burn-rate gates: - soft-burn (2x): trigger alerts and start shadow validation. - hard-burn (5x): enable tenant-level circuit breaker and prioritized throttling. 5) Shadow validation: replicate a configurable percent of live requests to a staging path where degradation policies execute; compare outputs and metrics to ensure quality regressions < threshold before enabling real-time throttle or model fallbacks.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: implement metric collection and per-tenant SLO config API (infra). Phase 1: pilot with 3 non-critical tenants; enable 1% shadow traffic, run for 2 weeks, record delta on quality_sli. Phase 2: enable soft-burn alerts and automated experiment orchestration for 10 pilot tenants. Phase 3: after pilot success, enable hard-burn enforcement for small subset (tiered: dev -> staging -> production tenants) with operator approval. Rollback: immediate disable of enforcement and revert to previous model variant; postmortem required if enforcement caused >5% unexpected error-rate increase across other tenants.
monitoring_and_alerting: - Dashboards: per-tenant SLI time-series (P50/P95/P99), composite SLO, error budget remaining, shadow-vs-prod delta. - Alerts: (A1) soft-burn alert when burn-rate > 2x for 6h; (A2) hard-burn alert when burn-rate > 5x for 15m; (A3) shadow divergence alert when quality delta > configured threshold for 1h; (A4) regional spillover alert when tenant failover increases downstream latency above 10% in target region. - Automated actions: soft-burn triggers notify on-call and schedule shadow-sample increase; hard-burn may flip tenant to degraded tier via automated runbook if approved.
circuit_breaker_policy: Tenant-level circuit breaker semantics: - Trip conditions: hard-burn OR availability_sli < 95% for 10m OR latency_p95 > 2x baseline for 5m. - Degradation steps: 1) Route to pinned lower-cost compatible model variant with reduced max_tokens; 2) Enable strict batching and KV-cache reuse for tenant routes; 3) Apply rate-limiter token-bucket at tenant route; 4) Evict non-essential background tasks tied to tenant. - Failover choreography: prefer regional failover within tenant's reserved region; if regional capacity insufficient, run prioritized cross-region failover with tenant isolation (do not borrow capacity from pinned enterprise slices). - Recovery: circuit breaker cool-down of 30m with progressive traffic ramp and continuous shadow validation to ensure quality.
acceptance_criteria: SLO schema documented in Confluence and linked from the SLO config API
Metric collection and per-tenant SLI dashboards deployed in Grafana with per-tenant filters
Shadow traffic pipeline implemented with sampling controls and data retention of 7d
Automated test that simulates burn-rate and verifies soft/hard gate behavior
Pilot run (3 tenants) shows <2% quality regression in shadow vs prod and documented runbook for hard-burn handling
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Shadow traffic might not reflect noisy real-world workloads -> Mitigation: sample representative requests using tenant traffic heuristics and augment with synthetic edge cases.
Risk: Too aggressive hard-burns could deny service -> Mitigation: require operator confirmation for first 3 hard-burns per tenant and provide automated rollback.
Risk: Metrics cardinality explosion by per-tenant SLIs -> Mitigation: enforce default tenant sampling, aggregate high-cardinality tags and offload long-term retention to metrics-archive tier.
